sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Chen Qianyu is a 5 -star character in Arknights: Endfield (AKE). Chen Qianyu wields a Sword and belongs to the Guard class. Chen Qianyu also has access to the Physical element. This guide provides a comprehensive overview of Chen Qianyu 's best build, including recommended Weapons, Gear pieces, Stats, and the strongest team compositions and rotations that maximize their potential.

 To learn more about Chen Qianyu check the sections below. Use the tabs to quickly switch to the kind of information you're looking for - whether it's best build, teams, synergies or calculations.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
"Well, turns out I'm great at something other than martial arts. I just can't help but end up as your best operator."
 Chen Qianyu is an operator at Endfield Industries and a core member of the Crisis Team.
 From a young age, she trained in martial arts under the guidance of her mother and at Tanjian Hall. Her dedication earned her outstanding combat capabilities and a mental fortitude rarely seen among her peers. Though she has never laid eyes on the legendary Chi Xiao, she proudly upholds her self-developed Chi Xiao Swordmancy, and wields it in the name of justice.
 After years of roaming Talos-II alone with her sword, Chen Qianyu joined Endfield at Perlica's invitation. Her upbeat nature and fierce enthusiasm drive her to tackle every urgent challenge without hesitation.

sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Free Vulnerability Infliction with combo.

 Above average Stagger across abilities and talent.

 Notable personal damage for a support damage dealer.

 Incredibly easy to trigger Combo Skill in any Physical team.

 Cheap Ultimate.

 She’s free!

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text: Cannot consume the Vulnerability stacks she generates, forcing her to play with a character that can.

sections.heading: Kit Intro
sections.text:
Chen is a 5-star, Physical, Sword support damage dealer who specializes in low-cost Vulnerable application while also outputting solid personal damage without the need to soak up the team's resources. Unlike Physical spenders like Endministrator or Da Pan, Chen has no way to spend Vulnerable herself, meaning teams are rarely built around her, and she’s slotted in as a combo piece in other characters' teams instead.
 The main reason to bring Chen to the team is her incredibly easy-to-activate Combo Skill, which only requires an enemy to become Vulnerable to activate, and which, on use, applies Lift and the Vulnerability stack that goes with it. Free application of Vulnerable is rare, and most Physical teams are starved for stacks and SP, making Chen a huge boon to the whole archetype.
 The other reason Chen is a solid inclusion in teams is her solid personal damage and good Stagger output. Due to applying Lift on both her combo and Battle Skill, they each inflict more Stagger than most characters, assuming the enemy already has Vulnerability stacks. Add to that the fact she has a solid personal ATK% buff talent, another talent which causes her to inflict even more Stagger when interrupting enemies during their telegraphed animations, and a low-cost Ultimate with good multipliers. Chen is definitely capable of contributing nicely to the team's overall output.

sections.heading: Combo
sections.text: Chen’s combo is her standout ability; it has a short cooldown and is very easy to activate, only requiring an enemy be afflicted with a stack of Vulnerable in order to trigger. Using it causes Chen to attack the target, inflicting Physical damage, and Lift. The snappy feedback of this combo and its ability to be used at any point during most Physical combos also makes it a strong ability for interrupting telegraphed enemy attack patterns.

sections.heading: Battle Skill
sections.text:
Chen’s Battle Skill is far less impressive than her combo, but still solid enough to use in some Physical team rotations. Using it costs 100 SP, deals Physical damage, some Stagger, and applies Lift. In teams without another character capable of applying Knock Down or Lift, and who only have other characters with Battle Skills that trigger Breach or Crush, its value does rise, though.
 That aside, the main reason to use this ability over other characters isn’t its damage, Stagger, or Vulnerability, as none of those are unique. Instead, it's to build and maintain stacks on one of Chen’s talents, which grants stacking ATK%.

sections.heading: Ultimate
sections.text:
Chen’s Ultimate is simply a large single-target Physical nuke with an above-average damage multiplier and Stagger amount. Using it causes Chen to lock onto a single target and perform a series of 6 small slashes followed by a large slash, which deals far more damage; each hit from this attack triggers on-hit effects.
 You can either use this ability's superior Stagger to push enemies into the Staggered state faster or save it for the Stagger window to take advantage of the Stagger damage multiplier and stats, such as DMG% vs Staggered enemies. A sub-stat common on Agility-based gear and many of Chen’s weapon choices.

sections.heading: Talents
sections.text:
Chen’s talents both contribute to her competent Stagger and damage output. The first, Slashing Edge, increases her damage by 8% for 10 seconds after she hits an enemy with a skill (Ultimate, Combo, or Battle Skill). The buff stacks up to 5 times for a maximum buff of 40% when capped out. When hitting multiple enemies with a single attack, each will grant a stack. Multi-hit abilities like Chen’s Ultimate also give stacks per hit.
 Tip: To maintain as high stacks as possible and for as long as possible, you can try to Stagger using Chen’s Battle Skill and Combo Skill slightly apart from each other.
 Chen’s other talent, Momentum Breaker, causes her to inflict an additional 10 Stagger when using her abilities to interrupt enemies' telegraphed abilities (big red rings). Given how Chen’s combo and Battle Skills are fast to execute, using them for this purpose isn’t too hard. It often won't interfere with most standard Physical team rotations, even if you have to save them for a bit. You don’t have to take advantage of this talent, but if you do, it’s a nice bonus.
 Note: Despite the wording, you have to use Chen’s abilities to interrupt enemies; you cannot use other characters and still get the bonus.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
How you play Chen will depend on the team you’re using her in, but across most teams, there is still a rough priority you can follow:
 Against enemies without Vulnerable, use another character’s Vulnerable application before Chen’s, as some characters require the first Vulnerability stack in order to gain bonuses/functionality. If this doesn’t apply, Chen can open up first with her Battle Skill instead.

 After applying the first stack of Vulnerable on enemies, if Chen’s combo is available, use it to add another.

 Optionally weave in Chen’s Battle Skill one or multiple times for additional Vulnerability stacks if your rotation needs them, and if you have the SP to spare. For those looking to optimize, try to space out Chen’s Battle Skill from her Combo Skill as much as possible without hurting your rotation to extend Slashing Edge’s duration.

 When Chen’s Ultimate is available, either save it for when the enemy is Staggered to maximize its damage or use it to push enemies into Stagger faster thanks to its higher Stagger value.

P 1

 An execute style damage increase for Chen, which helps in the second half of a fight but averages out to be around a generic 10% DMG% increase (Additive with other sources like Physical DMG%), which is solid but not a game changer.

 P 2

 A small boost to agility and some Physical DMG%, which adds together to be a modest but not particularly notable boost for Chen.

 P 3

 Dual-Wielding Swordmancer

 Boosts the damage of Chen’s Battle Skill, Combo Skill, and Ultimate by 10% (unique multiplier). This is Chen’s most impactful damage boosting potential so far, but also not a huge boost after factoring in Lift and passive basic attack damage.

 P 4
 Solo 123.09 %
 Team 106.1 %
 Improvised Chi Xiao

 Reduces Chen’s Ultimate cost by -15%, taking it from 70 to ~6,0 boosting the frequency of its use significantly, allowing you to output more damage but also more Stagger if you decide to use it outside the Stagger window.

 P 5
 Solo 123.09 %
 Team 106.1 %
 Bonded with the World

 Reduces Chen’s Combo Skill cooldown by 3 seconds. At maximum level, Chen’s Combo Skill has a 15-second cooldown, which is already short amongst most of the Physical damaging cast. Many Physical teams Chen is a part of work rotationally, where they each use all their combo and Battle Skills in sequence, effectively syncing up their cooldowns. Because of this, reducing Chen’s cooldown by 3 isn’t always as powerful as it sounds, as you’ll just be waiting on the next character’s Combo Skill cooldown in order to finish off your team's rotation. However, in some teams or strategies, you can make use of this extra cooldown reduction to either form new rotations or fit in extra Vulnerability stacks to existing rotations, making it a game-changer. Note: Calculations do not include the cooldown reduction of Chen’s Combo Skill, as the team used cannot benefit from it under the criteria we use.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Physical

 Endministrator Physical

 Applies a Vulnerability stack for free with Combo, allowing higher stack sizes to be much more efficiently achieved, leading to consistently higher Crush damage throughout the fight. This effect alone earns her a place in almost every Physical team.

 Higher than average Stagger across her kit

 Very capable Sub-DPS damage potential even with zero resources allocated to her

 Chen benefits nicely from Endmins teamwide buffs, boosting her damage further

 Pogranichnik Physical

 Applies a Vulnerability stack for free with Combo, allowing higher stack sizes to be much more efficiently achieved, leading to consistently higher Crush damage throughout the fight. This effect alone earns her a place in almost every Physical team.

 Higher than average Stagger across her kit

 Very capable Sub-DPS damage potential even with zero resources allocated to her

 Benefits nicely from Endmin’s teamwide buffs, boosting her damage further

 Physical

 Da Pan Physical

 Applies a Vulnerability stack for free with Combo, allowing higher stack sizes to be much more efficiently achieved. Without this help, Da Pan has a far, far harder time accessing his combo and successfully pulling off his game plan. This effect alone earns her a must-have place in Da Pan's teams.

 High than average Stagger across her kit

 Very capable sub DPS damage potential even with zero resources allocated to her

 Nature

 Ardelia Nature

 Able to permanently maintain both Arts and Physical susceptibility on targets for generic team-wide damage increases that work in any team

 Outstanding supportive weapon and set options for even more damage amplification, with options that work for both Physical and Arts

 Forcibly applies Corrosion, which, when optimized around, can lower enemy resistances to all damage temporarily if Susceptibility doesn't need to be refreshed

 Only requires 100 SP roughly every 30 seconds to function at maximum capacity

 Strong enough sustain to single handedly keep the team alive through most endgame encounters as long as smart dodging is used.

sections.heading: Ultimate timings
sections.text:
Endministrator - Use Endmin's Ultimate directly after their Combo Skill to ensure it consumes the Crystals to deal additional damage.
 Chen Qianyu - Use Chen's Ultimate after Endmin's Combo aswell - it doesn't apply Vulnerability or a Physical Status so it will gain the Crytals debuff without Shattering them, meaning Endmin's Battle Skill will still gain full value.
 Pogranichnik - Use Pog's Ultimate to gather enemies in AoE encounters and or before your main rotation to ensure you can consume stacks quickly.
 Ardelia - Save Ultimate for before one of your rotations, ideally during Stagger. Ardelia should be using Stanza Memoralis so using her Ultimate this way will buff the team.

sections.heading: Extra things to look out for
sections.text:
Against weaker enemies and those who struggle with sequencing all four characters at once, investing the time into establishing Ardelia's Combo Skill at the start of your rotation may not be worth it, instead you can skip it and go straight to your Physical rotation.
 Also against weaker enemies that may die in a single Crush/Breach, you can cut Chen's Battle Skill from the rotation to reduce its total cost to 200 SP instead of 300, making it immediately usable at the start of combat.
 Both the Endmin and Pog rotations can be interchanged in combat depending on what you need. If enemies are likely to last longer, you can apply Breach, but if they may die quickly, Crush might be more optimal.
 When playing Pog on Swordmancer and not using triggering Breach with his Battle Skill, the first Endmin Battle Skill can be swapped out for Pog's Battle Skill in order to weave in triggering Pog's Swordmancer passive.

 "Well, turns out I'm great at something other than martial arts. I just can't help but end up as your best operator."
 Chen Qianyu is an operator at Endfield Industries and a core member of the Crisis Team.
 From a young age, she trained in martial arts under the guidance of her mother and at Tanjian Hall. Her dedication earned her outstanding combat capabilities and a mental fortitude rarely seen among her peers. Though she has never laid eyes on the legendary Chi Xiao, she proudly upholds her self-developed Chi Xiao Swordmancy, and wields it in the name of justice.
 After years of roaming Talos-II alone with her sword, Chen Qianyu joined Endfield at Perlica's invitation. Her upbeat nature and fierce enthusiasm drive her to tackle every urgent challenge without hesitation.

 Pros & Cons

 Pros
 Free Vulnerability Infliction with combo.

 Above average Stagger across abilities and talent.

 Notable personal damage for a support damage dealer.

 Incredibly easy to trigger Combo Skill in any Physical team.

 Cons

 Review

 Kit Intro
 Chen is a 5-star, Physical, Sword support damage dealer who specializes in low-cost Vulnerable application while also outputting solid personal damage without the need to soak up the team's resources. Unlike Physical spenders like Endministrator or Da Pan, Chen has no way to spend Vulnerable herself, meaning teams are rarely built around her, and she’s slotted in as a combo piece in other characters' teams instead.
 The main reason to bring Chen to the team is her incredibly easy-to-activate Combo Skill, which only requires an enemy to become Vulnerable to activate, and which, on use, applies Lift and the Vulnerability stack that goes with it. Free application of Vulnerable is rare, and most Physical teams are starved for stacks and SP, making Chen a huge boon to the whole archetype.
 The other reason Chen is a solid inclusion in teams is her solid personal damage and good Stagger output. Due to applying Lift on both her combo and Battle Skill, they each inflict more Stagger than most characters, assuming the enemy already has Vulnerability stacks. Add to that the fact she has a solid personal ATK% buff talent, another talent which causes her to inflict even more Stagger when interrupting enemies during their telegraphed animations, and a low-cost Ultimate with good multipliers. Chen is definitely capable of contributing nicely to the team's overall output.
 Combo
 Chen’s combo is her standout ability; it has a short cooldown and is very easy to activate, only requiring an enemy be afflicted with a stack of Vulnerable in order to trigger. Using it causes Chen to attack the target, inflicting Physical damage, and Lift. The snappy feedback of this combo and its ability to be used at any point during most Physical combos also makes it a strong ability for interrupting telegraphed enemy attack patterns.
 Battle Skill
 Chen’s Battle Skill is far less impressive than her combo, but still solid enough to use in some Physical team rotations. Using it costs 100 SP, deals Physical damage, some Stagger, and applies Lift. In teams without another character capable of applying Knock Down or Lift, and who only have other characters with Battle Skills that trigger Breach or Crush, its value does rise, though.
 That aside, the main reason to use this ability over other characters isn’t its damage, Stagger, or Vulnerability, as none of those are unique. Instead, it's to build and maintain stacks on one of Chen’s talents, which grants stacking ATK%.
 Ultimate
 Chen’s Ultimate is simply a large single-target Physical nuke with an above-average damage multiplier and Stagger amount. Using it causes Chen to lock onto a single target and perform a series of 6 small slashes followed by a large slash, which deals far more damage; each hit from this attack triggers on-hit effects.
 You can either use this ability's superior Stagger to push enemies into the Staggered state faster or save it for the Stagger window to take advantage of the Stagger damage multiplier and stats, such as DMG% vs Staggered enemies. A sub-stat common on Agility-based gear and many of Chen’s weapon choices.
 Talents
 Chen’s talents both contribute to her competent Stagger and damage output. The first, Slashing Edge, increases her damage by 8% for 10 seconds after she hits an enemy with a skill (Ultimate, Combo, or Battle Skill). The buff stacks up to 5 times for a maximum buff of 40% when capped out. When hitting multiple enemies with a single attack, each will grant a stack. Multi-hit abilities like Chen’s Ultimate also give stacks per hit.
 Tip: To maintain as high stacks as possible and for as long as possible, you can try to Stagger using Chen’s Battle Skill and Combo Skill slightly apart from each other.
 Chen’s other talent, Momentum Breaker, causes her to inflict an additional 10 Stagger when using her abilities to interrupt enemies' telegraphed abilities (big red rings). Given how Chen’s combo and Battle Skills are fast to execute, using them for this purpose isn’t too hard. It often won't interfere with most standard Physical team rotations, even if you have to save them for a bit. You don’t have to take advantage of this talent, but if you do, it’s a nice bonus.
 Note: Despite the wording, you have to use Chen’s abilities to interrupt enemies; you cannot use other characters and still get the bonus.
 Gameplay
 How you play Chen will depend on the team you’re using her in, but across most teams, there is still a rough priority you can follow:
 Against enemies without Vulnerable, use another character’s Vulnerable application before Chen’s, as some characters require the first Vulnerability stack in order to gain bonuses/functionality. If this doesn’t apply, Chen can open up first with her Battle Skill instead.

 After applying the first stack of Vulnerable on enemies, if Chen’s combo is available, use it to add another.

 Optionally weave in Chen’s Battle Skill one or multiple times for additional Vulnerability stacks if your rotation needs them, and if you have the SP to spare. For those looking to optimize, try to space out Chen’s Battle Skill from her Combo Skill as much as possible without hurting your rotation to extend Slashing Edge’s duration.

 When Chen’s Ultimate is available, either save it for when the enemy is Staggered to maximize its damage or use it to push enemies into Stagger faster thanks to its higher Stagger value.
